headline: New US Data Centers Projected to Emit More Carbon Than All of Mexico
claim: AI data center buildout would erase about 15 years of US power-sector greenhouse gas reductions.
notes: published 2026-10-29; Bloomberg wire story (Eric Roston, Olivia Raimonde). Analysis is an internal Sierra Club estimate, an advocacy group (interested party); projections, not measured emissions. Figures: +618 million tons CO2 by 2030 (about 42%), mostly from off-grid gas. Bloomberg original page returned 403.

headline: US data center buildout risks erasing climate progress
claim: AI data center buildout would erase about 15 years of US power-sector greenhouse gas reductions.
notes: published 2026-10-28; Bloomberg wire story republished (Eric Roston, Olivia Raimonde). Analysis attributed to the Sierra Club, an advocacy group (interested party); projections, not measured emissions. Same figures as Bloomberg: +618 million tons CO2 by 2030 (about 42%).

headline: Report says new ChatGPT teen mode poses 'unacceptable risk' to youth safety
claim: ChatGPT's teen mode is an unacceptable risk to young people: it fails to alert parents when teens discuss self-harm and suicide.
notes: published 2026-10-27; WHYY story by Emily Swanson. Report by Common Sense Media (advocacy nonprofit, interested party); test-based assessment, not a peer-reviewed study. Report release date not stated in article (Bloomberg covered it 2026-10-07). OpenAI disputes the findings.

headline: New York Times and three other US papers sue Brave over AI scraping
claim: Brave scraped paywalled news articles, sold them to AI companies, and bypassed paywalls, harming publishers.
notes: published 2026-11-02; federal suit in Manhattan filed by NYT, Daily News, Chicago Tribune, Orlando Sentinel against Brave Software. Allegations only; no court has ruled. Plaintiffs are the publishers (interested parties). Article says the suits allege Brave sells its scraped index to Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI and Cohere.
